newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GWA expects lower first half profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GWA expects lower first half profit.

text.p: Bathroom products manufacturer GWA International Ltd said on Friday it expected its first half profit result to be about six to nine percent below the previous period.
The company said the lower first half forecast reflected reduced market demand for the quarter to September 1996.

"It is unlikely that the strong export drive which continues to grow revenue and profits for the Group will offset the lacklustre markets in Australia," GWA chairman Barry Thornton told shareholders at the annual meeting.

Thornton said that earnings before interest and tax to September 1996 had been impacted by the very low level of economic activity throughout Australia, a slow housing market and the lack of government spending at all levels.
He remained confident that the company was positioned well for any uptick in the domestic economy and was maintaining research and development and capital expenditure.

"The Group was well-placed to lift profitability when domestic demand recovers. GWA International has maintained research and development activity and new capital expenditures," Thornton said, adding that about A$4.7 million in capital expenditure had been approved in the first quarter.
GWA shares closed two cents higher at A$2.16 on turnover of 2.41 million shares.
